newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle lower, awaits USDA report.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle lower, awaits USDA report.

text.p: FCOJ futures were hit by late selling to end lower despite the market already being oversold and ripe for a modest recovery according to some traders.
On Thursday the USDA will release its latest Florida crop estimate at 0830 EST before the market opens, but traders and analysts said no surprises were expected.
In USDA's December report it forecast a 1996/97 crop of 220 million boxes.

"No change is expected, that seems to be the consensus," analyst Bernard Savaiko of PaineWebber said. "This market is grossly oversold and that might temper any bearish ideas following the report. Most of the selling has been done."
March futures settled 1.40 cents weaker at 80.10 cents per pound, traded 81.80 to 80.00 cents.
Volume was estimated at 3,500 lots compared to Tuesday's official 2,386 lots.
But one trader said the market probably needed to fall a little further to trigger technical indicators to find a bottom before retracing.
Fears of damaging cold weather hitting the Florida citrus belt also receded further Wednesday, taking away some supportive sentiment, traders said.
